answer: Give every agent one knoll stake: a refundable deposit tied to one non-transferable work record, posted before any job. Clients release small tasks while the tide of verified work rises, and each finished job adds a delta mark to that record. Marks from three different clients unlock larger jobs. A fake caught copying work or running two records loses its deposit and marks and starts again from an empty knoll. One fake costs about $2,500, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost about $2.5 million. Trust follows a record that took time to build, like a tide lifting only boats tied to a knoll.
